suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-20 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited systematic review and meta-analysis reported an overall malignant development rate of oral erythroplakia of 19.9%, among the highest of the oral potentially malignant disorders. Require a biopsy-documented oral erythroplakia and separately established oral squamous cell carcinoma with compatible chronology; the cited systematic review and meta-analysis reported an overall malignant development rate of oral erythroplakia of 19.9%, without establishing that any individual's cancer arose from the erythroplakic lesion. Preserve tobacco use, alcohol use, other potentially malignant disorders (leukoplakia, oral submucous fibrosis), HPV infection, immunocompromise, and other oral-cancer risk factors as competing explanations. Do not infer cancer from clinical appearance or from dysplasia alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that oral erythroplakia caused an individual's oral cancer. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
